1	// This file implements lossless archiving of one organization's audit
2	// export. AuditExport hands back detached in-memory records and the caller
3	// separately retains the checkpoint pinning them; an archive serializes the
4	// export so it can be saved to a file when the service instance ends and
5	// read back later, still paired with the caller's own checkpoint and still
6	// usable as the material for RecheckDecisionOffline.
7	//
8	// The format is a length-delimited binary encoding built by hand rather
9	// than encoding/json: JSON text cannot carry bytes that are not valid
10	// UTF-8 without silently replacing them with U+FFFD, which would collapse
11	// genuinely different content (a lone 0xFF, a lone 0xFE and a real U+FFFD)
12	// onto identical records and change their fingerprints. Every string is
13	// written from its exact bytes with a length prefix, and nil slices,
14	// non-nil empty slices and absent payloads are each marked explicitly.
15	//
16	// Integrity never comes from trust in the file. A decode reconstructs the
17	// records and then runs the same whole-material VerifyAudit chain check
18	// against the checkpoint the caller supplies independently; the checkpoint
19	// embedded in the archive is informational only and never authoritative.
20	package darksafe
21	
22	import (
23		"bytes"
24		"crypto/sha256"
25		"encoding/binary"
26		"errors"
27		"fmt"
28	)
29	
30	// ErrInvalidArchive means archive bytes are not a recognizable, complete,
31	// untampered audit archive: a foreign/truncated/trailing-byte framing, a
32	// failed checksum, or content that does not decode. Content-level failures
33	// (missing or mismatched organization, missing, out-of-order or modified
34	// records, a mismatched checkpoint) keep using ErrMissingOrganization and
35	// ErrInvalidRange exactly as the other audit entry points do.
36	var ErrInvalidArchive = errors.New("darksafe: invalid audit archive")
37	
38	// Archive framing:
39	//
40	//	magic   = archiveMagic
41	//	u32 BE  = byte length of the payload that follows
42	//	payload = archivePayloadLen bytes
43	//	32 bytes = SHA-256 checksum of payload
44	//
45	// A second archive concatenated to a first is trailing material, not a
46	// second frame: a read consumes exactly one frame and rejects any byte
47	// beyond it.
48	const archiveMagic = "darksafe-audit-archive-v1\n"
49	
50	const (
51		archiveTagBoolFalse byte = 0
52		archiveTagBoolTrue  byte = 1
53		archiveTagNil       byte = 0
54		archiveTagPresent   byte = 1
55	)
56	
57	// archiveWriter appends length-delimited fields to a byte buffer.
58	type archiveWriter struct {
59		buf []byte
60		err error
61	}
62	
63	func (w *archiveWriter) raw(data []byte) {
64		w.buf = append(w.buf, data...)
65	}
66	
67	// u32 writes a non-negative int as a big-endian uint32.
68	func (w *archiveWriter) u32(v int) {
69		if v < 0 || uint64(v) > 0xffffffff {
70			w.err = fmt.Errorf("%w: length out of range: %d", ErrInvalidArchive, v)
71			return
72		}
73		var b [4]byte
74		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(b[:], uint32(v))
75		w.buf = append(w.buf, b[:]...)
76	}
77	
78	func (w *archiveWriter) boolean(v bool) {
79		if v {
80			w.buf = append(w.buf, archiveTagBoolTrue)
81		} else {
82			w.buf = append(w.buf, archiveTagBoolFalse)
83		}
84	}
85	
86	// put appends one raw framing byte. It is the archive sink's side of the
87	// shared list shape: the list presence marker (archiveTagNil for nil,
88	// archiveTagPresent for a non-nil list) goes into the payload verbatim.
89	func (w *archiveWriter) put(b byte) {
90		w.buf = append(w.buf, b)
91	}
92	
93	// listCount writes a list element count through the archive's own
94	// range-checked u32, so a list length the uint32 format cannot represent
95	// still fails the whole archive with the existing ErrInvalidArchive rather
96	// than emitting truncated framing or returning partial bytes.
97	func (w *archiveWriter) listCount(n int) {
98		w.u32(n)
99	}
100	
101	// stringField writes a string from its exact memory bytes. Nothing is
102	// validated, replaced or normalized: a lone 0xFF reaches the output as
103	// itself and stays distinguishable from 0xFE and a genuine U+FFFD.
104	func (w *archiveWriter) stringField(s string) {
105		w.u32(len(s))
106		if w.err != nil {
107			return
108		}
109		w.buf = append(w.buf, s...)
110	}
111	
112	// policy writes one Policy by walking the single policy field table, so the
113	// archive's field order is the fingerprint's order by construction. Even the
114	// fingerprint-optional ResourceID is always written here (empty included),
115	// so every field round trips on its own; its placement is fixed by the
116	// table and therefore cannot move a fingerprint boundary.
117	func (w *archiveWriter) policy(p Policy) {
118		for i := range policyFields {
119			f := &policyFields[i]
120			switch f.kind {
121			case policyFieldString, policyFieldOptionalString:
122				w.stringField(f.getString(p))
123			case policyFieldBool:
124				w.boolean(f.getBool(p))
125			}
126		}
127	}
128	
129	// change writes the policy-change payload, or a single absence marker:
130	// VerifyAudit only ever accepts a change payload on a policy-change record
131	// and its absence otherwise, but the distinction is encoded explicitly so
132	// decode never has to reconstruct a shape. A present payload walks the
133	// single policy-change field table, so the archive's field order is the
134	// fingerprint's order by construction and every change field round trips.
135	func (w *archiveWriter) change(c *PolicyChange) {
136		if c == nil {
137			w.buf = append(w.buf, archiveTagNil)
138			return
139		}
140		w.buf = append(w.buf, archiveTagPresent)
141		for i := range changeFields {
142			f := &changeFields[i]
143			switch f.kind {
144			case changeFieldInt:
145				w.u32(f.getInt(c))
146			case changeFieldPolicyList:
147				writeListShape(w, f.getPolicies(c), w.policy)
148			case changeFieldBool:
149				w.boolean(f.getBool(c))
150			}
151		}
152	}
153	
154	// decisionRecord writes the decision payload, or a single absence marker:
155	// VerifyAudit only ever accepts a decision payload on a decision record and
156	// its absence otherwise, but the distinction is encoded explicitly so decode
157	// never has to reconstruct a shape. A present payload walks the single
158	// decision field table, so the archive's field order is the fingerprint's
159	// order by construction and every request and decision field round trips.
160	func (w *archiveWriter) decisionRecord(d *DecisionRecord) {
161		if d == nil {
162			w.buf = append(w.buf, archiveTagNil)
163			return
164		}
165		w.buf = append(w.buf, archiveTagPresent)
166		for i := range decisionFields {
167			f := &decisionFields[i]
168			switch f.kind {
169			case decisionFieldString:
170				w.stringField(f.getString(d))
171			case decisionFieldStringList:
172				writeListShape(w, f.getList(d), w.stringField)
173			case decisionFieldBool:
174				w.boolean(f.getBool(d))
175			case decisionFieldInt:
176				w.u32(f.getInt(d))
177			}
178		}
179	}
180	
181	// EncodeAuditArchive serializes one complete audit export into savable
182	// bytes. org is the organization name, records is its complete chain from
183	// sequence 1 (a valid prefix ending at some historical sequence is enough,
184	// provided cp pins exactly that sequence), and cp is the checkpoint the
185	// caller separately retains. An organization with no records archives too:
186	// records is empty and cp is its sequence-0 genesis checkpoint.
187	//
188	// The whole material is validated exactly as VerifyAudit would before any
189	// bytes are returned: a missing organization is ErrMissingOrganization, and
190	// a missing, out-of-order or foreign record, modified content or checkpoint
191	// mismatch is ErrInvalidRange. On failure no archive bytes are returned.
192	// The checkpoint is carried in the archive for reference, but never stands
193	// in for the separately retained evidence: DecodeAuditArchive always
194	// validates against the checkpoint handed to it. The call is read-only:
195	// neither the records nor any service state are mutated and no audit record
196	// is appended.
197	func EncodeAuditArchive(org string, records []AuditRecord, cp Checkpoint) ([]byte, error) {
198		if org == "" {
199			return nil, ErrMissingOrganization
200		}
201		if err := VerifyAudit(org, records, cp); err != nil {
202			return nil, err
203		}
204	
205		pw := &archiveWriter{}
206		pw.stringField(org)
207		pw.u32(cp.EndSeq)
208		pw.stringField(cp.Fingerprint)
209		pw.u32(len(records))
210		for i := range records {
211			rec := &records[i]
212			// The outer record fields walk the single record field table, so
213			// the archive's record layout is the fingerprint envelope's layout
214			// — plus the record's own fingerprint, which the envelope excludes
215			// — by construction, and no outer field can be skipped or
216			// reordered here alone.
217			for j := range recordFields {
218				f := &recordFields[j]
219				switch f.kind {
220				case recordFieldString:
221					pw.stringField(f.getString(rec))
222				case recordFieldInt:
223					pw.u32(f.getInt(rec))
224				case recordFieldChange:
225					pw.change(f.getChange(rec))
226				case recordFieldDecision:
227					pw.decisionRecord(f.getDecision(rec))
228				}
229			}
230		}
231		if pw.err != nil {
232			return nil, pw.err
233		}
234		payload := pw.buf
235	
236		out := make([]byte, 0, len(archiveMagic)+4+len(payload)+sha256.Size)
237		out = append(out, archiveMagic...)
238		var lenBuf [4]byte
239		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(lenBuf[:], uint32(len(payload)))
240		out = append(out, lenBuf[:]...)
241		out = append(out, payload...)
242		sum := sha256.Sum256(payload)
243		out = append(out, sum[:]...)
244		return out, nil
245	}
246	
247	// archiveReader walks one payload without copying string contents: string
248	// fields are backed by the payload slice itself, which is owned by the
249	// decoder and never returned, so callers cannot mutate the input through
250	// the result.
251	type archiveReader struct {
252		data []byte
253		pos  int
254		err  error
255	}
256	
257	func (r *archiveReader) need(n int) bool {
258		if r.err != nil {
259			return false
260		}
261		if n < 0 || r.pos > len(r.data)-n {
262			r.err = fmt.Errorf("%w: truncated archive payload", ErrInvalidArchive)
263			return false
264		}
265		return true
266	}
267	
268	func (r *archiveReader) marker() byte {
269		if !r.need(1) {
270			return 0
271		}
272		b := r.data[r.pos]
273		r.pos++
274		return b
275	}
276	
277	func (r *archiveReader) u32() int {
278		if !r.need(4) {
279			return 0
280		}
281		v := int(binary.BigEndian.Uint32(r.data[r.pos : r.pos+4]))
282		r.pos += 4
283		return v
284	}
285	
286	// boundedCount reads a count and proves at least minBytesPerItem bytes
287	// remain per item, so a hostile payload cannot drive a huge allocation
288	// with a count its body could never satisfy.
289	func (r *archiveReader) boundedCount(minBytesPerItem int) int {
290		n := r.u32()
291		if r.err != nil {
292			return 0
293		}
294		if n < 0 || uint64(n)*uint64(minBytesPerItem) > uint64(len(r.data)-r.pos) {
295			r.err = fmt.Errorf("%w: implausible list count %d", ErrInvalidArchive, n)
296			return 0
297		}
298		return n
299	}
300	
301	func (r *archiveReader) boolean() bool {
302		switch r.marker() {
303		case archiveTagBoolTrue:
304			return true
305		case archiveTagBoolFalse:
306			return false
307		default:
308			if r.err == nil {
309				r.err = fmt.Errorf("%w: invalid boolean marker", ErrInvalidArchive)
310			}
311			return false
312		}
313	}
314	
315	func (r *archiveReader) stringField() string {
316		n := r.u32()
317		if r.err != nil {
318			return ""
319		}
320		if !r.need(n) {
321			return ""
322		}
323		// Conversion copies the bytes, so the result never aliases the input.
324		s := string(r.data[r.pos : r.pos+n])
325		r.pos += n
326		return s
327	}
328	
329	// readList reads one length-counted list framed by writeListShape on the
330	// archive sink, whatever its item type: both string lists and the policy
331	// list decode here. Every list
332	// kind gets the exact same framing checks — the nil/presence marker, the
333	// per-item byte floor before any allocation, and each item's own
334	// truncation/structure errors — so a hostile count can neither drive a
335	// disproportionate allocation nor deliver a partial list: once an item
336	// fails, the reader's sticky error fails the whole read.
337	// minBytesPerItem is the minimum an item could occupy (each string item
338	// carries one length word; a policy item carries six length words and a
339	// bool), and is used only to reject counts the remaining bytes could never
340	// satisfy.
341	func readList[T any](r *archiveReader, minBytesPerItem int, readItem func() T) []T {
342		switch r.marker() {
343		case archiveTagNil:
344			return nil
345		case archiveTagPresent:
346		default:
347			if r.err == nil {
348				r.err = fmt.Errorf("%w: invalid list marker", ErrInvalidArchive)
349			}
350			return nil
351		}
352		n := r.boundedCount(minBytesPerItem)
353		if r.err != nil {
354			return nil
355		}
356		items := make([]T, n)
357		for i := range items {
358			items[i] = readItem()
359		}
360		return items
361	}
362	
363	func (r *archiveReader) policy() Policy {
364		// Read fields in the single table's (write and fingerprint) order. The
365		// fingerprint-optional ResourceID is still a mandatory, fixed field on
366		// the archive, so it is read for every policy including the empty one.
367		var p Policy
368		for i := range policyFields {
369			f := &policyFields[i]
370			switch f.kind {
371			case policyFieldString, policyFieldOptionalString:
372				f.setString(&p, r.stringField())
373			case policyFieldBool:
374				f.setBool(&p, r.boolean())
375			}
376		}
377		return p
378	}
379	
380	func (r *archiveReader) change() *PolicyChange {
381		switch r.marker() {
382		case archiveTagNil:
383			return nil
384		case archiveTagPresent:
385		default:
386			if r.err == nil {
387				r.err = fmt.Errorf("%w: invalid change payload marker", ErrInvalidArchive)
388			}
389			return nil
390		}
391		// Read fields in the single table's (write and fingerprint) order, so a
392		// field can never be restored into the wrong member or skipped.
393		c := &PolicyChange{}
394		for i := range changeFields {
395			f := &changeFields[i]
396			switch f.kind {
397			case changeFieldInt:
398				f.setInt(c, r.u32())
399			case changeFieldPolicyList:
400				// A policy writes six length words (five strings plus
401				// ResourceID) and one bool byte at minimum.
402				f.setPolicies(c, readList(r, 6*4+1, r.policy))
403			case changeFieldBool:
404				f.setBool(c, r.boolean())
405			}
406		}
407		return c
408	}
409	
410	func (r *archiveReader) decisionRecord() *DecisionRecord {
411		switch r.marker() {
412		case archiveTagNil:
413			return nil
414		case archiveTagPresent:
415		default:
416			if r.err == nil {
417				r.err = fmt.Errorf("%w: invalid decision payload marker", ErrInvalidArchive)
418			}
419			return nil
420		}
421		// Read fields in the single table's (write and fingerprint) order, so a
422		// field can never be restored into the wrong member or skipped.
423		d := &DecisionRecord{}
424		for i := range decisionFields {
425			f := &decisionFields[i]
426			switch f.kind {
427			case decisionFieldString:
428				f.setString(d, r.stringField())
429			case decisionFieldStringList:
430				// Each string item carries at least one length word.
431				f.setList(d, readList(r, 4, r.stringField))
432			case decisionFieldBool:
433				f.setBool(d, r.boolean())
434			case decisionFieldInt:
435				f.setInt(d, r.u32())
436			}
437		}
438		return d
439	}
440	
441	// decodedArchiveFrame is one archive parsed up to, but not including, the
442	// content checks: the reconstructed records and the informational
443	// checkpoint embedded in the header. Nothing at this stage has been
444	// validated against the caller's organization or retained checkpoint.
445	type decodedArchiveFrame struct {
446		records     []AuditRecord
447		org         string
448		endSeq      int
449		fingerprint string
450	}
451	
452	// decodeAuditArchiveFrame parses one frame's framing, checksum and payload.
453	// It performs no content validation: the embedded organization and
454	// checkpoint are returned for the caller to compare, and the records are
455	// not chain-checked until a content-validating entry point runs the single
456	// VerifyAudit pass.
457	func decodeAuditArchiveFrame(archive []byte) (decodedArchiveFrame, error) {
458		magicLen := len(archiveMagic)
459		if len(archive) < magicLen+4+sha256.Size || string(archive[:magicLen]) != archiveMagic {
460			return decodedArchiveFrame{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: unrecognized audit archive", ErrInvalidArchive)
461		}
462		pos := magicLen
463		payloadLen := int(binary.BigEndian.Uint32(archive[pos : pos+4]))
464		pos += 4
465		checksumEnd := pos + payloadLen
466		if payloadLen < 0 || checksumEnd+sha256.Size != len(archive) {
467			// A short frame is truncation; bytes beyond the one frame (a
468			// concatenated second archive, junk appended to a good file) are a
469			// framing failure too.
470			return decodedArchiveFrame{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: truncated or trailing audit archive bytes", ErrInvalidArchive)
471		}
472		payload := archive[pos:checksumEnd]
473		sum := sha256.Sum256(payload)
474		if !bytes.Equal(sum[:], archive[checksumEnd:checksumEnd+sha256.Size]) {
475			return decodedArchiveFrame{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: checksum mismatch", ErrInvalidArchive)
476		}
477	
478		r := &archiveReader{data: payload}
479		embeddedOrg := r.stringField()
480		embeddedEndSeq := r.u32()
481		embeddedFingerprint := r.stringField()
482		// Every record writes two payload markers, a sequence word, two
483		// fingerprint length words and org/kind length words: 22 bytes even
484		// when every string is empty.
485		n := r.boundedCount(22)
486		if r.err != nil {
487			return decodedArchiveFrame{}, r.err
488		}
489		records := make([]AuditRecord, 0, n)
490		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
491			// Read the outer fields in the single record field table's (write
492			// and fingerprint) order, so a field can never be restored into the
493			// wrong member or skipped.
494			var rec AuditRecord
495			for j := range recordFields {
496				f := &recordFields[j]
497				switch f.kind {
498				case recordFieldString:
499					f.setString(&rec, r.stringField())
500				case recordFieldInt:
501					f.setInt(&rec, r.u32())
502				case recordFieldChange:
503					f.setChange(&rec, r.change())
504				case recordFieldDecision:
505					f.setDecision(&rec, r.decisionRecord())
506				}
507			}
508			records = append(records, rec)
509		}
510		if r.err != nil {
511			return decodedArchiveFrame{}, r.err
512		}
513		if r.pos != len(payload) {
514			return decodedArchiveFrame{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: %d unconsumed archive bytes", ErrInvalidArchive, len(payload)-r.pos)
515		}
516		return decodedArchiveFrame{
517			records:     records,
518			org:         embeddedOrg,
519			endSeq:      embeddedEndSeq,
520			fingerprint: embeddedFingerprint,
521		}, nil
522	}
523	
524	// validateDecodedFrame applies the content checks to a parsed frame and
525	// returns the material as VerifiedAuditMaterial after the single complete
526	// VerifyAudit chain pass. The embedded checkpoint is informational; still,
527	// contradicting the retained checkpoint means the payload was altered, and
528	// the authoritative check always uses the caller's independently retained
529	// checkpoint.
530	func validateDecodedFrame(frame decodedArchiveFrame, org string, cp Checkpoint) (VerifiedAuditMaterial, error) {
531		// Content checks reuse the exact audit-range validation the live export
532		// and offline review paths use, so an archive can never smuggle in a
533		// shape those entry points would reject.
534		if frame.org != org {
535			return VerifiedAuditMaterial{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: archive organization %q does not match %q", ErrInvalidRange, frame.org, org)
536		}
537		if frame.endSeq != cp.EndSeq || frame.fingerprint != cp.Fingerprint {
538			return VerifiedAuditMaterial{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: embedded checkpoint does not match the retained checkpoint", ErrInvalidRange)
539		}
540		return verifyAuditMaterial(org, frame.records, cp)
541	}
542	
543	// DecodeVerifiedAuditArchive reads one archive produced by
544	// EncodeAuditArchive, validates it once, and returns the material ready
545	// for RecheckVerifiedDecisionOffline. It is the single-validation half of
546	// the offline review flow: the returned VerifiedAuditMaterial carries the
547	// already-checked chain, so the following review performs no second chain
548	// pass. org is the organization the caller expects, and cp is the
549	// checkpoint the caller independently retained; the checkpoint embedded in
550	// the file is never treated as evidence, so even an archive carrying a
551	// plausible checkpoint only validates against the one supplied here.
552	//
553	// A missing organization is ErrMissingOrganization. Unrecognized framing,
554	// truncation, a trailing second archive or any other extra byte, a bad
555	// checksum, and undecodable content are ErrInvalidArchive. Records that
556	// decode but are missing, out of order, foreign to the organization,
557	// modified (including a record after the one the caller intends to review)
558	// or mismatched with the supplied checkpoint fail the whole read with
559	// ErrInvalidRange. Failure returns no material. A successful read only
560	// proves the material matches the checkpoint: an original decision that
561	// disagrees with a recomputed one is reported later by offline review, not
562	// treated as archive damage. The material is detached from archive
563	// (mutating one never reaches the other), and the call is read-only.
564	func DecodeVerifiedAuditArchive(archive []byte, org string, cp Checkpoint) (VerifiedAuditMaterial, error) {
565		if org == "" {
566			return VerifiedAuditMaterial{}, ErrMissingOrganization
567		}
568		frame, err := decodeAuditArchiveFrame(archive)
569		if err != nil {
570			return VerifiedAuditMaterial{}, err
571		}
572		return validateDecodedFrame(frame, org, cp)
573	}
574	
575	// DecodeAuditArchive reads one archive produced by EncodeAuditArchive and
576	// returns records that can be handed directly to RecheckDecisionOffline.
577	// org is the organization the caller expects, and cp is the checkpoint the
578	// caller independently retained; the checkpoint embedded in the file is
579	// never treated as evidence, so even an archive carrying a plausible
580	// checkpoint only validates against the one supplied here.
581	//
582	// This is a standalone entry point: it performs the complete archive and
583	// chain validation itself and never assumes another entry point ran first.
584	// (The `darksafe review` command instead uses DecodeVerifiedAuditArchive
585	// followed by RecheckVerifiedDecisionOffline, so one invocation validates
586	// the chain exactly once rather than once here and again in the review.)
587	//
588	// A missing organization is ErrMissingOrganization. Unrecognized framing,
589	// truncation, a trailing second archive or any other extra byte, a bad
590	// checksum, and undecodable content are ErrInvalidArchive. Records that
591	// decode but are missing, out of order, foreign to the organization,
592	// modified (including a record after the one the caller intends to review)
593	// or mismatched with the supplied checkpoint fail the whole read with
594	// ErrInvalidRange. Failure returns no records. A successful read only
595	// proves the material matches the checkpoint: an original decision that
596	// disagrees with a recomputed one is reported later by offline review, not
597	// treated as archive damage. The result is detached from archive (mutating
598	// one never reaches the other), and the call is read-only.
599	func DecodeAuditArchive(archive []byte, org string, cp Checkpoint) ([]AuditRecord, error) {
600		m, err := DecodeVerifiedAuditArchive(archive, org, cp)
601		if err != nil {
602			return nil, err
603		}
604		return m.records, nil
605	}

1	// This file implements the organization-scoped audit chain. Every successful
2	// policy publish or rollback, and every Decide called with a non-empty
3	// decision organization, leaves an immutable record in that organization.
4	//
5	// Records carry an organization-local sequence starting at 1 and a SHA-256
6	// fingerprint that chains each record to the previous one. The genesis
7	// fingerprint binds the organization name, so records from another
8	// organization can never validate as part of this chain even when the
9	// sequence numbers and identifiers coincide.
10	package darksafe
11	
12	import (
13		"crypto/sha256"
14		"encoding/binary"
15		"encoding/hex"
16		"encoding/json"
17		"errors"
18		"fmt"
19	)
20	
21	// Audit record categories.
22	const (
23		// AuditPolicyChange is a successful publish or rollback.
24		AuditPolicyChange = "policy_change"
25		// AuditDecision is one Decide evaluation.
26		AuditDecision = "decision"
27	)
28	
29	// Sentinel errors for the audit entry points. Callers distinguish them
30	// with errors.Is; every one leaves state unchanged.
31	var (
32		// ErrInvalidPage means a page size or range argument was invalid.
33		ErrInvalidPage = errors.New("darksafe: invalid audit page")
34		// ErrInvalidRange means the upper bound is beyond what exists, the
35		// range is inverted, or a supplied fingerprint does not match.
36		ErrInvalidRange = errors.New("darksafe: invalid audit range")
37		// ErrAuditNotFound means no record exists at the requested sequence.
38		ErrAuditNotFound = errors.New("darksafe: audit record not found")
39		// ErrAuditNotADecision means the record at the sequence is not a
40		// decision record and therefore cannot be rechecked.
41		ErrAuditNotADecision = errors.New("darksafe: audit record is not a decision")
42	)
43	
44	// PolicyChange captures a successful publish or rollback.
45	type PolicyChange struct {
46		// Version is the newly created policy version.
47		Version int
48		// Policies is the full policy set of the new version.
49		Policies []Policy
50		// SourceVersion is the version copied by a rollback, and 0 for an
51		// ordinary publish.
52		SourceVersion int
53		// RolledBack reports whether the change was produced by Rollback.
54		RolledBack bool
55	}
56	
57	// DecisionRecord captures one Decide call: the full request and the
58	// decision actually returned.
59	type DecisionRecord struct {
60		Request  OrgRequest
61		Decision Decision
62	}
63	
64	// AuditRecord is one immutable entry in an organization's audit chain.
65	type AuditRecord struct {
66		Org      string
67		Seq      int // organization-local, starting at 1 and gapless
68		Kind     string
69		Change   *PolicyChange   // present when Kind == AuditPolicyChange
70		Decision *DecisionRecord // present when Kind == AuditDecision
71	
72		// PrevFingerprint is the fingerprint of the preceding record, or the
73		// genesis fingerprint for the first record.
74		PrevFingerprint string
75		// Fingerprint binds this record's full content to its predecessor.
76		Fingerprint string
77	}
78	
79	// rawEnvelopePrefix opens every raw-byte canonical encoding. It never
80	// coincides with the start of a JSON envelope (always '{'), so
81	// fingerprints from the two encodings live in collision-free spaces.
82	const rawEnvelopePrefix = "darksafe-audit-raw-v1\x00"
83	
84	// fingerprintTag delimits one field or nested value within the canonical
85	// binary encoding. Distinct tags keep two payloads that merely share
86	// adjacent bytes apart (e.g. ["ab",""] vs ["a","b"]).
87	type fingerprintTag byte
88	
89	const (
90		tagEnvelope fingerprintTag = iota + 1
91		tagSeq
92		tagString
93		tagStringList
94		tagBool
95		tagPolicy
96		tagPolicyList
97		tagChange
98		tagSubject
99		tagResource
100		tagDecision
101		tagDecisionRecord
102	)
103	
104	// fingerprintEncoder builds the canonical byte representation of an
105	// envelope. Unlike encoding/json it writes string contents byte-for-byte
106	// with an explicit length prefix, so strings carrying invalid UTF-8 stay
107	// distinguishable: encoding/json renders both a raw 0xFF byte and a raw
108	// 0xFE byte as the U+FFFD replacement rune, collapsing genuinely
109	// different content onto identical fingerprints.
110	type fingerprintEncoder struct {
111		buf []byte
112	}
113	
114	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) tag(t fingerprintTag) {
115		e.buf = append(e.buf, byte(t))
116	}
117	
118	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) int64Tag(t fingerprintTag, v int64) {
119		e.tag(t)
120		var b [8]byte
121		binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(b[:], uint64(v))
122		e.buf = append(e.buf, b[:]...)
123	}
124	
125	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) boolTag(t fingerprintTag, v bool) {
126		e.tag(t)
127		if v {
128			e.buf = append(e.buf, 1)
129		} else {
130			e.buf = append(e.buf, 0)
131		}
132	}
133	
134	// rawString tags and writes a string from its exact memory bytes. No
135	// validation, replacement or normalization is ever performed: an invalid
136	// UTF-8 byte reaches the hash unchanged.
137	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) rawString(s string) {
138		e.tag(tagString)
139		var b [4]byte
140		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(b[:], uint32(len(s)))
141		e.buf = append(e.buf, b[:]...)
142		e.buf = append(e.buf, s...)
143	}
144	
145	// put appends one raw framing byte. It is the fingerprint sink's side of the
146	// shared list shape: the list presence marker goes into the canonical bytes
147	// verbatim.
148	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) put(b byte) {
149		e.buf = append(e.buf, b)
150	}
151	
152	// listCount writes a list element count as a big-endian uint32. The raw
153	// canonical encoding has no length ceiling beyond the hash input, so unlike
154	// the archive sink the count is written unconditionally; only the list shape
155	// (nil marker, presence marker, count then one item per element) is shared.
156	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) listCount(n int) {
157		var b [4]byte
158		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(b[:], uint32(n))
159		e.buf = append(e.buf, b[:]...)
160	}
161	
162	// stringList preserves nil-vs-empty explicitly: in the JSON envelope a
163	// nil slice is "null" and a non-nil empty slice is "[]", so the raw
164	// encoding must keep the two shapes apart as well. The list's own kind tag
165	// leads, then the shared list shape carries the presence marker, count and
166	// elements under it.
167	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) stringList(items []string) {
168		e.tag(tagStringList)
169		writeListShape(e, items, e.rawString)
170	}
171	
172	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) policy(p Policy) {
173		e.tag(tagPolicy)
174		// Field order, the Recursive boolean's position, and ResourceID being
175		// appended only when set all come from the single policy field table, so
176		// the fingerprint and the archive enumerate fields in exactly one place.
177		for i := range policyFields {
178			f := &policyFields[i]
179			switch f.kind {
180			case policyFieldString:
181				e.rawString(f.getString(p))
182			case policyFieldOptionalString:
183				// ResourceID participates only when set, pairing with its
184				// omitempty JSON tag, so the legacy fingerprint bytes are
185				// unchanged for resource-unrestricted policies.
186				if v := f.getString(p); v != "" {
187					e.rawString(v)
188				}
189			case policyFieldBool:
190				e.boolTag(tagBool, f.getBool(p))
191			}
192		}
193	}
194	
195	// policyList frames the full policy set with the shared list shape, led by
196	// the policy-list tag so a policy set can never collide with a string list
197	// whose concatenated bytes happen to match.
198	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) policyList(policies []Policy) {
199		e.tag(tagPolicyList)
200		writeListShape(e, policies, e.policy)
201	}
202	
203	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) change(c *PolicyChange) {
204		e.tag(tagChange)
205		// A nil pointer is encoded as tagChange alone; a present value's
206		// fields follow immediately.
207		if c == nil {
208			return
209		}
210		// Field order comes from the single policy-change field table, so the
211		// fingerprint, the UTF-8 decision, the archive and the detaching copy
212		// enumerate fields in exactly one place. No change field is skipped.
213		for i := range changeFields {
214			f := &changeFields[i]
215			switch f.kind {
216			case changeFieldInt:
217				e.int64Tag(tagSeq, int64(f.getInt(c)))
218			case changeFieldPolicyList:
219				e.policyList(f.getPolicies(c))
220			case changeFieldBool:
221				e.boolTag(tagBool, f.getBool(c))
222			}
223		}
224	}
225	
226	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) decisionRecord(d *DecisionRecord) {
227		e.tag(tagDecisionRecord)
228		if d == nil {
229			return
230		}
231		// Field order and the subject/resource/decision group markers all come
232		// from the single decision field table, so the fingerprint, the UTF-8
233		// decision and the archive enumerate fields in exactly one place. No
234		// request or decision field is skipped.
235		for i := range decisionFields {
236			f := &decisionFields[i]
237			if f.groupTag != 0 {
238				e.tag(f.groupTag)
239			}
240			switch f.kind {
241			case decisionFieldString:
242				e.rawString(f.getString(d))
243			case decisionFieldStringList:
244				e.stringList(f.getList(d))
245			case decisionFieldBool:
246				e.boolTag(tagBool, f.getBool(d))
247			case decisionFieldInt:
248				e.int64Tag(tagSeq, int64(f.getInt(d)))
249			}
250		}
251	}
252	
253	// encodeCanonical returns the raw bytes fingerprinted for a record whose
254	// strings include invalid UTF-8. Every string the record carries reaches
255	// the output byte-for-byte, at whatever nesting depth or list position it
256	// occupies. The prefix separates this encoding space from JSON
257	// fingerprints. The outer fields come from the single record field table,
258	// so this encoding enumerates exactly the envelope members the JSON
259	// encoding and the valid-UTF-8 scan see, in the same order.
260	func encodeCanonical(r *AuditRecord) []byte {
261		e := &fingerprintEncoder{buf: []byte(rawEnvelopePrefix)}
262		e.tag(tagEnvelope)
263		for i := range recordFields {
264			f := &recordFields[i]
265			if f.jsonKey == "" {
266				// The record's own fingerprint is never an input to itself.
267				continue
268			}
269			switch f.kind {
270			case recordFieldString:
271				e.rawString(f.getString(r))
272			case recordFieldInt:
273				e.int64Tag(tagSeq, int64(f.getInt(r)))
274			case recordFieldChange:
275				e.change(f.getChange(r))
276			case recordFieldDecision:
277				e.decisionRecord(f.getDecision(r))
278			}
279		}
280		return e.buf
281	}

283	// genesisFingerprint derives the chain root from the organization name,
284	// keeping equal identifiers in different organizations independent.
285	func genesisFingerprint(org string) string {
286		sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte("darksafe-audit-genesis\x00" + org))
287		return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
288	}
289	
290	// encodeJSONEnvelope renders the fingerprint envelope of a record whose
291	// strings are all valid UTF-8 as the exact byte sequence the historical
292	// encoding/json envelope struct produced: the envelope members in the
293	// single record field table's order, every string, integer and payload
294	// encoded by encoding/json itself, and the two payload members dropped
295	// when absent exactly as their historical omitempty tags did. Walking the
296	// table keeps this object in lockstep with the raw canonical encoding, the
297	// valid-UTF-8 scan and the archive framing by construction.
298	func encodeJSONEnvelope(r *AuditRecord) []byte {
299		var buf []byte
300		buf = append(buf, '{')
301		first := true
302		for i := range recordFields {
303			f := &recordFields[i]
304			if f.jsonKey == "" {
305				// The record's own fingerprint is never an input to itself.
306				continue
307			}
308			var (
309				value []byte
310				err   error
311			)
312			switch f.kind {
313			case recordFieldString:
314				value, err = json.Marshal(f.getString(r))
315			case recordFieldInt:
316				value, err = json.Marshal(f.getInt(r))
317			case recordFieldChange:
318				c := f.getChange(r)
319				if c == nil {
320					continue
321				}
322				value, err = json.Marshal(c)
323			case recordFieldDecision:
324				d := f.getDecision(r)
325				if d == nil {
326					continue
327				}
328				value, err = json.Marshal(d)
329			}
330			if err != nil {
331				// All envelope values are plain, JSON-encodable values; a
332				// failure here indicates a programming error, not user input.
333				panic(fmt.Errorf("darksafe: audit envelope must encode: %w", err))
334			}
335			if !first {
336				buf = append(buf, ',')
337			}
338			first = false
339			buf = append(buf, '"')
340			buf = append(buf, f.jsonKey...)
341			buf = append(buf, '"', ':')
342			buf = append(buf, value...)
343		}
344		return append(buf, '}')
345	}
346	
347	// fingerprintFor returns the fingerprint for a record. Records made
348	// exclusively of valid UTF-8 keep the historical JSON fingerprint, so old
349	// exports and checkpoints remain valid; records containing invalid bytes
350	// use the length-prefixed raw encoding that protects their exact bytes.
351	// Both families cover exactly the envelope members of the single record
352	// field table — never the record's own fingerprint.
353	func fingerprintFor(r *AuditRecord) string {
354		if recordUsesRawBytes(r) {
355			sum := sha256.Sum256(encodeCanonical(r))
356			return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
357		}
358		sum := sha256.Sum256(encodeJSONEnvelope(r))
359		return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
360	}

362	// clonePolicies returns a detached copy of a policy set.
363	func clonePolicies(in []Policy) []Policy {
364		if in == nil {
365			return nil
366		}
367		return append([]Policy(nil), in...)
368	}

370	// cloneChange returns a detached copy of a policy-change payload.
371	func cloneChange(c *PolicyChange) *PolicyChange {
372		if c == nil {
373			return nil
374		}
375		cp := *c
376		// Detach every list the single policy-change field table carries; the
377		// per-list nil-versus-empty handling stays exactly as clonePolicies
378		// defines it.
379		cloneChangeLists(&cp, c)
380		return &cp
381	}
382	
383	// cloneStrings returns a detached copy of a string slice while preserving
384	// its nil-versus-empty shape: a nil slice stays nil, and every non-nil
385	// slice, including a non-nil empty slice that still carries spare capacity,
386	// receives its own backing array. Copying only when len > 0 is not enough:
387	// a caller may submit make([]string, 0, 4), and aliasing that array into a
388	// stored record would let an append to one handed-out copy overwrite the
389	// first element of every other copy that shares it.
390	func cloneStrings(in []string) []string {
391		if in == nil {
392			return nil
393		}
394		return append([]string{}, in...)
395	}
396	
397	// cloneDecision returns a detached copy of a decision payload.
398	func cloneDecision(d *DecisionRecord) *DecisionRecord {
399		if d == nil {
400			return nil
401		}
402		cp := *d
403		// Detach every list the single decision field table carries, on non-nil
404		// rather than on len > 0 so empty-but-capacious lists are independent
405		// copies too; nil lists stay nil.
406		cloneDecisionLists(&cp, d)
407		return &cp
408	}

410	// cloneRecord returns a fully detached copy of a record.
411	func cloneRecord(r *AuditRecord) *AuditRecord {
412		cp := *r
413		cp.Change = cloneChange(r.Change)
414		cp.Decision = cloneDecision(r.Decision)
415		return &cp
416	}

418	// appendAuditLocked validates, fingerprints and stores one record. It runs
419	// under the store mutex and is the single place records are created.
420	func (st *orgState) appendAuditLocked(org, kind string, change *PolicyChange, decision *DecisionRecord) *AuditRecord {
421		seq := len(st.audit) + 1
422		prev := genesisFingerprint(org)
423		if len(st.audit) > 0 {
424			prev = st.audit[len(st.audit)-1].Fingerprint
425		}
426		// Store detached copies; later caller mutation must not reach the chain.
427		rec := &AuditRecord{
428			Org:             org,
429			Seq:             seq,
430			Kind:            kind,
431			Change:          cloneChange(change),
432			Decision:        cloneDecision(decision),
433			PrevFingerprint: prev,
434		}
435		rec.Fingerprint = fingerprintFor(rec)
436		st.audit = append(st.audit, rec)
437		return cloneRecord(rec)
438	}

440	// auditHeadLocked returns the highest sequence in the chain and the
441	// fingerprint that covers it: (0, genesis) for an organization with no
442	// records.
443	func (st *orgState) auditHeadLocked(org string) (int, string) {
444		if len(st.audit) == 0 {
445			return 0, genesisFingerprint(org)
446		}
447		last := st.audit[len(st.audit)-1]
448		return last.Seq, last.Fingerprint
449	}

451	// Checkpoint pins an audit query to an exact point in a chain.
452	type Checkpoint struct {
453		Org         string
454		EndSeq      int
455		Fingerprint string
456	}
457	
458	// AuditPage is one stable slice of an organization's audit chain.
459	type AuditPage struct {
460		Org     string
461		Records []AuditRecord
462		// BeginSeq/EndSeq delimit the whole pinned range, not just this page.
463		BeginSeq int
464		EndSeq   int
465		// Next is the first sequence of the following page, 0 when exhausted.
466		Next int
467		// Checkpoint is the pinned upper bound shared by every page.
468		Checkpoint Checkpoint
469	}
470	
471	// recordMatches reports whether a record survives the query filters. Every
472	// set filter is a conjunction: kind, subject and resource conditions must
473	// all hold. Empty filter values mean "not set".
474	func recordMatches(r *AuditRecord, kind, subjectID, resourceID string) bool {
475		if kind != "" && r.Kind != kind {
476			return false
477		}
478		if subjectID != "" {
479			// A subject filter selects decision records of that subject only.
480			if r.Kind != AuditDecision || r.Decision == nil ||
481				r.Decision.Request.Subject.ID != subjectID {
482				return false
483			}
484		}
485		if resourceID != "" {
486			// A resource filter selects decision records whose request named
487			// exactly this resource. Policy-change records never match, even when
488			// a published policy carries the identical ResourceID: the condition
489			// reads the requested resource, not policy content. The comparison is
490			// Go string equality over the stored raw bytes, so case, surrounding
491			// and internal spaces, control bytes and invalid UTF-8 are all
492			// significant, and no path or wildcard is interpreted.
493			if r.Kind != AuditDecision || r.Decision == nil ||
494				r.Decision.Request.Resource.ID != resourceID {
495				return false
496			}
497		}
498		return true
499	}
500	
501	// optionalResourceCondition extracts the optional resource condition passed
502	// as the trailing variadic argument. An absent argument or an empty string
503	// means "no resource filter"; supplying more than one condition is a caller
504	// error rather than a silently picked value.
505	func optionalResourceCondition(conds []string) (string, error) {
506		switch len(conds) {
507		case 0:
508			return "", nil
509		case 1:
510			return conds[0], nil
511		default:
512			return "", fmt.Errorf("%w: at most one resource condition may be set, got %d", ErrInvalidPage, len(conds))
513		}
514	}
515	
516	// AuditQuery pins the first page of an audit query. startSeq is the first
517	// sequence considered (1 from the beginning); endSeq <= 0 means "everything
518	// currently stored". The returned checkpoint must be passed to AuditPage
519	// for the following pages, so records appended after the first query never
520	// mix into later pages.
521	//
522	// kind and subjectID are the existing optional filters (empty means unset):
523	// kind selects a record category and subjectID selects one subject's
524	// decision records. The optional trailing resourceID adds a resource
525	// condition, empty or absent meaning unset: only decision records whose
526	// requested resource ID equals it byte-for-byte survive — case sensitive,
527	// spaces and control bytes significant, no path or wildcard interpretation,
528	// invalid UTF-8 kept as-is — and policy-change records never survive it,
529	// even when a published policy names the same resource ID. Every set
530	// condition applies together. A resource filter changes only which records
531	// are returned: paging, checkpoints and detached copies behave exactly as
532	// without it, and omitting it preserves the historical call and its results.
533	func (s *Store) AuditQuery(org string, startSeq, pageSize int, kind, subjectID string, resourceID ...string) (*AuditPage, error) {
534		resource, err := optionalResourceCondition(resourceID)
535		if err != nil {
536			return nil, err
537		}
538		if org == "" {
539			return nil, ErrMissingOrganization
540		}
541		if kind != "" && kind != AuditPolicyChange && kind != AuditDecision {
542			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: unknown category %q", ErrInvalidPage, kind)
543		}
544		if pageSize <= 0 {
545			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: page size must be positive, got %d", ErrInvalidPage, pageSize)
546		}
547		if startSeq < 1 {
548			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: start sequence must be >= 1, got %d", ErrInvalidPage, startSeq)
549		}
550		s.mu.Lock()
551		defer s.mu.Unlock()
552		st := s.orgLocked(org)
553		end, fingerprint := st.auditHeadLocked(org)
554		cp := Checkpoint{Org: org, EndSeq: end, Fingerprint: fingerprint}
555		if end == 0 {
556			// An organization with no records always yields the empty genesis
557			// page, regardless of where the caller asked to begin.
558			return &AuditPage{Org: org, BeginSeq: 1, EndSeq: 0, Checkpoint: cp}, nil
559		}
560		if startSeq > end {
561			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: start sequence %d is beyond end sequence %d", ErrInvalidRange, startSeq, end)
562		}
563		return s.auditPageLocked(org, startSeq, end, fingerprint, pageSize, kind, subjectID, resource), nil
564	}
565	
566	// AuditPage returns one page of a previously pinned query. nextSeq is the
567	// cursor from the previous page; when it is 0 the range is exhausted. The
568	// checkpoint is re-verified against the chain on every call.
569	//
570	// The filters are the same as AuditQuery's and must agree with the pinned
571	// query: pass the same kind, subjectID and optional resourceID on every
572	// page. The resource condition is an exact raw-byte match over requested
573	// resource IDs and excludes policy-change records, exactly as on the first
574	// page; omitting it keeps the historical call and result shape.
575	func (s *Store) AuditPage(cp Checkpoint, nextSeq, pageSize int, kind, subjectID string, resourceID ...string) (*AuditPage, error) {
576		resource, err := optionalResourceCondition(resourceID)
577		if err != nil {
578			return nil, err
579		}
580		if cp.Org == "" {
581			return nil, ErrMissingOrganization
582		}
583		if kind != "" && kind != AuditPolicyChange && kind != AuditDecision {
584			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: unknown category %q", ErrInvalidPage, kind)
585		}
586		if pageSize <= 0 {
587			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: page size must be positive, got %d", ErrInvalidPage, pageSize)
588		}
589		if nextSeq < 0 {
590			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: next sequence must be >= 0, got %d", ErrInvalidPage, nextSeq)
591		}
592		s.mu.Lock()
593		defer s.mu.Unlock()
594		st, ok := s.orgs[cp.Org]
595		if !ok {
596			// No organization state: the only valid checkpoint is an empty one.
597			g := genesisFingerprint(cp.Org)
598			if cp.EndSeq == 0 && cp.Fingerprint == g && nextSeq == 0 {
599				return &AuditPage{Org: cp.Org, BeginSeq: 0, EndSeq: 0, Checkpoint: cp}, nil
600			}
601			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: checkpoint organization has no records", ErrInvalidRange)
602		}
603		head := len(st.audit)
604		if cp.EndSeq < 0 || cp.EndSeq > head {
605			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: end sequence %d beyond %d", ErrInvalidRange, cp.EndSeq, head)
606		}
607		wantFP := genesisFingerprint(cp.Org)
608		if cp.EndSeq > 0 {
609			if cp.EndSeq > len(st.audit) {
610				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: end sequence %d beyond %d", ErrInvalidRange, cp.EndSeq, head)
611			}
612			wantFP = st.audit[cp.EndSeq-1].Fingerprint
613		}
614		if cp.Fingerprint != wantFP {
615			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: checkpoint fingerprint does not match the chain at sequence %d", ErrInvalidRange, cp.EndSeq)
616		}
617		if nextSeq == 0 {
618			return &AuditPage{Org: cp.Org, BeginSeq: 1, EndSeq: cp.EndSeq, Checkpoint: cp}, nil
619		}
620		if nextSeq > cp.EndSeq+1 {
621			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: next sequence %d beyond pinned range ending at %d", ErrInvalidRange, nextSeq, cp.EndSeq)
622		}
623		if nextSeq == cp.EndSeq+1 {
624			return &AuditPage{Org: cp.Org, BeginSeq: nextSeq, EndSeq: cp.EndSeq, Checkpoint: cp}, nil
625		}
626		return s.auditPageLocked(cp.Org, nextSeq, cp.EndSeq, wantFP, pageSize, kind, subjectID, resource), nil
627	}
628	
629	// auditPageLocked scans forward collecting up to pageSize matching records
630	// and computes the next-page cursor. It does not stop at pageSize raw
631	// records: filtering happens within the pinned [start,end] window, so
632	// non-matching records between matches — including policy changes excluded
633	// by a resource condition — never consume page slots.
634	func (s *Store) auditPageLocked(org string, startSeq, endSeq int, endFP string, pageSize int, kind, subjectID, resourceID string) *AuditPage {
635		st := s.orgs[org]
636		// pageSize only bounds how many records this page returns; it must not
637		// drive allocation. A caller may pass any positive value, including the
638		// largest int, for a range holding a handful of records, so preallocate
639		// no more than the window can actually contain.
640		window := endSeq - startSeq + 1
641		capHint := pageSize
642		if window < capHint {
643			capHint = window
644		}
645		out := make([]AuditRecord, 0, capHint)
646		i := startSeq
647		for ; i <= endSeq && len(out) < pageSize; i++ {
648			r := st.audit[i-1]
649			if recordMatches(r, kind, subjectID, resourceID) {
650				out = append(out, *cloneRecord(r))
651			}
652		}
653		next := 0
654		if i <= endSeq {
655			next = i
656		}
657		return &AuditPage{
658			Org:        org,
659			Records:    out,
660			BeginSeq:   startSeq,
661			EndSeq:     endSeq,
662			Next:       next,
663			Checkpoint: Checkpoint{Org: org, EndSeq: endSeq, Fingerprint: endFP},
664		}
665	}
666	
667	// AuditExport returns detached copies of the complete records through
668	// endSeq, suitable for offline verification. endSeq <= 0 means everything
669	// currently stored. An organization with no records yields an empty slice
670	// together with its sequence-0 checkpoint.
671	func (s *Store) AuditExport(org string, endSeq int) (records []AuditRecord, cp Checkpoint, err error) {
672		if org == "" {
673			return nil, Checkpoint{}, ErrMissingOrganization
674		}
675		s.mu.Lock()
676		defer s.mu.Unlock()
677		st := s.orgLocked(org)
678		head := len(st.audit)
679		if endSeq <= 0 {
680			endSeq = head
681		}
682		if endSeq > head {
683			return nil, Checkpoint{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: end sequence %d beyond %d", ErrInvalidRange, endSeq, head)
684		}
685		if endSeq < 0 {
686			return nil, Checkpoint{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: end sequence must be >= 0, got %d", ErrInvalidPage, endSeq)
687		}
688		// The checkpoint fingerprints the final exported record, not the
689		// possibly later current head.
690		fingerprint := genesisFingerprint(org)
691		if endSeq > 0 {
692			fingerprint = st.audit[endSeq-1].Fingerprint
693		}
694		out := make([]AuditRecord, 0, endSeq)
695		for i := 0; i < endSeq; i++ {
696			out = append(out, *cloneRecord(st.audit[i]))
697		}
698		return out, Checkpoint{Org: org, EndSeq: endSeq, Fingerprint: fingerprint}, nil
699	}
700	
701	// VerifyAudit validates an exported record set entirely without a Store.
702	// The caller separately retains the organization, end sequence and
703	// fingerprint they expect. It rejects any modified field, missing middle or
704	// tail record, swapped order, and record spliced in from another
705	// organization. Empty or nil records validate exactly when the checkpoint
706	// is the organization's genesis (end sequence 0).
707	func VerifyAudit(org string, records []AuditRecord, cp Checkpoint) error {
708		if org == "" {
709			return ErrMissingOrganization
710		}
711		if cp.Org != "" && cp.Org != org {
712			return fmt.Errorf("%w: checkpoint organization %q does not match %q", ErrInvalidRange, cp.Org, org)
713		}
714		genesis := genesisFingerprint(org)
715		if len(records) == 0 {
716			if cp.EndSeq != 0 || cp.Fingerprint != genesis {
717				return fmt.Errorf("%w: empty records but checkpoint claims end sequence %d", ErrInvalidRange, cp.EndSeq)
718			}
719			return nil
720		}
721		if cp.EndSeq != len(records) {
722			return fmt.Errorf("%w: have %d records, checkpoint ends at %d", ErrInvalidRange, len(records), cp.EndSeq)
723		}
724		prev := genesis
725		for i, r := range records {
726			wantSeq := i + 1
727			if r.Org != org {
728				return fmt.Errorf("%w: record %d belongs to organization %q", ErrInvalidRange, wantSeq, r.Org)
729			}
730			if r.Seq != wantSeq {
731				return fmt.Errorf("%w: record %d has sequence %d", ErrInvalidRange, wantSeq, r.Seq)
732			}
733			if r.PrevFingerprint != prev {
734				return fmt.Errorf("%w: record %d breaks the chain", ErrInvalidRange, wantSeq)
735			}
736			wantFP := fingerprintFor(&r)
737			if r.Fingerprint != wantFP {
738				return fmt.Errorf("%w: record %d fingerprint mismatch", ErrInvalidRange, wantSeq)
739			}

788		resolve := func(version int) versionPolicies {
789			src, ok := st.versions[version]
790			if !ok {
791				// A decision's version is immutable and never deleted; its
792				// absence indicates store tampering rather than normal
793				// operation.
794				return versionPolicies{status: replayVersionAbsent}
795			}
796			// Live snapshots are immutable; detach anyway so the returned
797			// decision can never share storage with the store.
798			return versionPolicies{policies: append([]Policy(nil), src...)}
799		}
800		d, status := replayRecordedDecision(org, req, version, resolve)
801		if status == replayVersionAbsent {
802			return Decision{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: decision used version %d, which no longer exists", ErrVersionNotFound, version)

1	// This file is the single definition of which outer fields an AuditRecord
2	// carries for every audit-side treatment of record-envelope content: the
3	// fingerprint's JSON and raw canonical encoders, the valid-UTF-8 test that
4	// chooses between the two fingerprint families, and the archive writer and
5	// reader. Each of those walks the one table below instead of naming the
6	// fields itself, so the fields and their order mean the same thing
7	// everywhere. Adding or changing an outer record field here reaches
8	// fingerprinting, the UTF-8 decision, archiving and unarchiving at once; no
9	// audit path can keep a stale list of its own.
10	//
11	// The table order is part of the wire and fingerprint contract: it is the
12	// historical envelope order — organization, sequence, category, the two
13	// payloads, the previous fingerprint — followed by the record's own
14	// fingerprint, which the archive stores but the fingerprint itself never
15	// covers. The contents of the two payloads stay governed by their own
16	// field tables (policy, policy-change and decision); this table only names
17	// which payload sits where in the envelope.
18	package darksafe
19	
20	import "unicode/utf8"
21	
22	// recordFieldKind says how one outer AuditRecord field participates in
23	// fingerprinting and archiving.
24	type recordFieldKind int
25	
26	const (
27		// recordFieldString is a string field written from its exact bytes by
28		// the raw fingerprint encoder and the archive, and encoded as a JSON
29		// string by the legacy fingerprint family.
30		recordFieldString recordFieldKind = iota
31		// recordFieldInt is a non-negative integer field (the sequence number).
32		// It has no UTF-8 representation, so the valid-UTF-8 scan skips it
33		// while both encoders write it.
34		recordFieldInt
35		// recordFieldChange is the policy-change payload slot. Its nil-versus-
36		// present shape is marked explicitly by the raw encoder and the
37		// archive, and omitted from the JSON envelope when absent; which change
38		// content is protected remains decided by the policy-change field
39		// table.
40		recordFieldChange
41		// recordFieldDecision is the decision payload slot, treated exactly
42		// like the policy-change slot; which decision content is protected
43		// remains decided by the decision field table.
44		recordFieldDecision
45	)
46	
47	// recordFieldSpec locates one outer AuditRecord field. The accessors used
48	// depend on the kind: string fields use getString/setString, the sequence
49	// uses getInt/setInt and the payload slots getChange/setChange and
50	// getDecision/setDecision. A field appears in recordFields exactly once,
51	// and that entry is the only place its struct member is named.
52	type recordFieldSpec struct {
53		kind recordFieldKind
54		// jsonKey is the field's name in the legacy JSON fingerprint envelope
55		// and doubles as the envelope-membership marker: every field up to and
56		// including the previous fingerprint has one, while the record's own
57		// fingerprint has none, because a fingerprint can never be an input to
58		// itself. The archive writes every field, envelope member or not.
59		jsonKey     string
60		getString   func(*AuditRecord) string
61		setString   func(*AuditRecord, string)
62		getInt      func(*AuditRecord) int
63		setInt      func(*AuditRecord, int)
64		getChange   func(*AuditRecord) *PolicyChange
65		setChange   func(*AuditRecord, *PolicyChange)
66		getDecision func(*AuditRecord) *DecisionRecord
67		setDecision func(*AuditRecord, *DecisionRecord)
68	}

71	// order, which the archive reproduces exactly and then extends with the
72	// record's own fingerprint: Org, Seq, Kind, Change, Decision,
73	// PrevFingerprint, Fingerprint, exactly as the historical encodings placed
74	// them.

76		{
77			kind:      recordFieldString,
78			jsonKey:   "org",
79			getString: func(r *AuditRecord) string { return r.Org },

93		},

99		},

104			setDecision: func(r *AuditRecord, d *DecisionRecord) { r.Decision = d },
105		},

108			jsonKey:   "prev",
109			getString: func(r *AuditRecord) string { return r.PrevFingerprint },
110			setString: func(r *AuditRecord, s string) { r.PrevFingerprint = s },

377					Request:  request("acme", "u1", "r1", "org/a", "read"),
378					Decision: Decision{Allowed: true, Reason: "matched allow policy", Matched: []string{"p1"}, Version: 1},
379				}
380			},
381			// Spaces, Chinese, control characters and a lone non-UTF-8 byte.
382			func(seq int) (string, *PolicyChange, *DecisionRecord) {
383				return AuditDecision, nil, &DecisionRecord{
384					Request:  request("acme", "u3", "r1", "org/a", "read"),
385					Decision: Decision{Allowed: false, Reason: rawReason, Version: 1},
386				}
387			},
388			// An explicitly empty reason.
389			func(seq int) (string, *PolicyChange, *DecisionRecord) {
390				return AuditDecision, nil, &DecisionRecord{
391					Request:  request("acme", "u4", "r1", "org/a", "read"),
392					Decision: Decision{Allowed: false, Reason: emptyReason, Version: 1},
393				}
394			},
395			// A genuine U+FFFD must stay distinct from the lone 0xFF above.
396			func(seq int) (string, *PolicyChange, *DecisionRecord) {
397				return AuditDecision, nil, &DecisionRecord{
398					Request:  request("acme", "u5", "r1", "org/a", "read"),
399					Decision: Decision{Allowed: false, Reason: genuineReplacement, Version: 1},
400				}
401			},
402		})
403	
404		archive, err := EncodeAuditArchive("acme", recs, cp)
405		if err != nil {
406			t.Fatalf("encode valid reasons: %v", err)
407		}
408		got, err := DecodeAuditArchive(archive, "acme", cp)
409		if err != nil {
410			t.Fatalf("decode valid reasons: %v", err)
411		}
412		if !reflect.DeepEqual(got, recs) {
413			t.Fatalf("valid reasons changed across the archive:\n got %+v\nwant %+v", got, recs)
414		}
415	
416		// Byte-for-byte reason assertions; length is understood in bytes.
417		wantReasons := []string{"matched allow policy", rawReason, emptyReason, genuineReplacement}
418		for i, want := range wantReasons {
419			if gotReason := got[i+1].Decision.Decision.Reason; gotReason != want {
420				t.Fatalf("record %d reason = %q, want %q", i+2, gotReason, want)
421			}
422		}
423		if got[3].Decision.Decision.Reason != "" {
424			t.Fatal("empty reason must decode as the empty string, not absent or replaced")
425		}
426		// The raw-byte reason and the genuine-U+FFFD reason must not collapse.
427		if got[2].Decision.Decision.Reason == got[4].Decision.Decision.Reason {
428			t.Fatal("lone 0xFF reason and genuine U+FFFD reason collapsed together")
429		}
430		if !strings.Contains(got[2].Decision.Decision.Reason, invalidByte) {
431			t.Fatal("non-UTF-8 reason byte was replaced or normalized")
432		}
433	
434		// Fingerprints/checkpoint unchanged and the material still verifies.
435		for i := range got {
436			if got[i].Fingerprint != recs[i].Fingerprint {
437				t.Fatalf("record %d fingerprint changed", i+1)
438			}
439		}
440		if err := VerifyAudit("acme", got, cp); err != nil {
441			t.Fatalf("decoded valid-reason material must verify: %v", err)
442		}
443		// The canonical decision in the same material remains offline-reviewable.
444		review, err := RecheckDecisionOffline("acme", got, cp, 2)
445		if err != nil || !review.Consistent || review.Original.Reason != "matched allow policy" {
446			t.Fatalf("offline review after reason round trip = %+v, %v", review, err)
447		}
448	}

1	// This file pins down the decoder's handling of corrupted *internal list
2	// lengths*: archives whose outer framing, declared payload length and
3	// checksum are all correct, but where a count declared inside the payload
4	// cannot be satisfied by the bytes that follow. Three lists carry counts:
5	// the material's record list, a policy change's policy list, and the string
6	// lists used for subject roles and matched policies.
7	//
8	// Every corruption below is reframed with a consistent outer length and
9	// checksum, so exercising these cases proves the protection comes from
10	// decoding the payload's own structure rather than from the framing-level
11	// samples in audit_archive_test.go. A count the body cannot satisfy, a
12	// count word cut off mid-read, and a complete early item followed by an
13	// incomplete later item are all unreadable archives: DecodeAuditArchive
14	// must return ErrInvalidArchive (matched by errors.Is) and nil records,
15	// never a prefix and never a crash or hostile allocation.
16	package darksafe
17	
18	import (
19		"bytes"
20		"crypto/sha256"
21		"encoding/binary"
22		"errors"
23		"reflect"
24		"runtime"
25		"strings"
26		"testing"
27	)
28	
29	// listSite locates one length-counted list inside a payload, in payload
30	// byte offsets. itemEnds marks the byte just past each complete item.
31	type listSite struct {
32		markerAt int
33		countAt  int // -1 when the list is encoded nil
34		itemEnds []int
35	}
36	
37	// payloadInspector walks the known-good, two-record fixture payload in
38	// encode order. It exists only to locate the bytes a test corrupts; it
39	// mirrors archiveWriter, so a format change moves these tests off their
40	// target rather than silently corrupting the wrong field.
41	type payloadInspector struct {
42		b   []byte
43		pos int
44	}
45	
46	func (c *payloadInspector) u32() int {
47		v := int(binary.BigEndian.Uint32(c.b[c.pos : c.pos+4]))
48		c.pos += 4
49		return v
50	}
51	
52	func (c *payloadInspector) str() {
53		n := c.u32()
54		c.pos += n
55	}
56	
57	func (c *payloadInspector) marker() byte {
58		m := c.b[c.pos]
59		c.pos++
60		return m
61	}
62	
63	func (c *payloadInspector) stringListSite() listSite {
64		s := listSite{markerAt: c.pos, countAt: -1}
65		if c.marker() == archiveTagNil {
66			return s
67		}
68		s.countAt = c.pos
69		n := c.u32()
70		s.itemEnds = make([]int, 0, n)
71		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
72			c.str()
73			s.itemEnds = append(s.itemEnds, c.pos)
74		}
75		return s
76	}
77	
78	func (c *payloadInspector) policySite() {
79		c.str() // ID
80		c.str() // Subject
81		c.str() // Action
82		c.str() // Scope
83		c.str() // Effect
84		c.pos++ // Recursive bool
85		c.str() // ResourceID
86	}
87	
88	func (c *payloadInspector) policyListSite() listSite {
89		s := listSite{markerAt: c.pos, countAt: -1}
90		if c.marker() == archiveTagNil {
91			return s
92		}
93		s.countAt = c.pos
94		n := c.u32()
95		s.itemEnds = make([]int, 0, n)
96		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
97			c.policySite()
98			s.itemEnds = append(s.itemEnds, c.pos)
99		}
100		return s
101	}
102	
103	// inspectTwoRecordPayload locates the four counted lists in the fixture
104	// built by listCorruptionFixture.
105	func inspectTwoRecordPayload(t *testing.T, p []byte) fixtureSites {
106		t.Helper()
107		c := &payloadInspector{b: p}
108		c.str()    // embedded org
109		c.pos += 4 // embedded end sequence
110		c.str()    // embedded checkpoint fingerprint
111		records := listSite{countAt: c.pos}
112		n := c.u32() // record count
113		if n != 2 {
114			t.Fatalf("fixture record count = %d, want 2", n)
115		}
116	
117		// Record 1: policy change with two policies, absent decision.
118		c.str()    // org
119		c.pos += 4 // seq
120		c.str()    // kind
121		if m := c.marker(); m != archiveTagPresent {
122			t.Fatalf("record 1 change marker = %d, want present", m)
123		}
124		c.pos += 4 // change version
125		policies := c.policyListSite()
126		c.pos += 4 // source version
127		c.pos++    // rolled back bool
128		if m := c.marker(); m != archiveTagNil {
129			t.Fatalf("record 1 decision marker = %d, want nil", m)
130		}
131		c.str() // prev fingerprint
132		c.str() // own fingerprint
133		records.itemEnds = append(records.itemEnds, c.pos)
134	
135		// Record 2: decision with two roles and two matched policies.
136		c.str()    // org
137		c.pos += 4 // seq
138		c.str()    // kind
139		if m := c.marker(); m != archiveTagNil {
140			t.Fatalf("record 2 change marker = %d, want nil", m)
141		}
142		if m := c.marker(); m != archiveTagPresent {
143			t.Fatalf("record 2 decision marker = %d, want present", m)
144		}
145		c.str() // request SubjectOrg
146		c.str() // request ResourceOrg
147		c.str() // subject ID
148		c.str() // subject Kind
149		roles := c.stringListSite()
150		c.pos++ // subject disabled bool
151		c.str() // resource ID
152		c.str() // resource scope
153		c.str() // action
154		c.pos++ // decision allowed bool
155		c.str() // decision reason
156		matched := c.stringListSite()
157		c.pos += 4 // decision version
158		c.str()    // prev fingerprint
159		c.str()    // own fingerprint
160		records.itemEnds = append(records.itemEnds, c.pos)
161	
162		if c.pos != len(p) {
163			t.Fatalf("inspector ended at %d, payload length %d", c.pos, len(p))
164		}
165		if len(roles.itemEnds) != 2 || len(matched.itemEnds) != 2 || len(policies.itemEnds) != 2 {
166			t.Fatalf("fixture lists must each hold 2 items: policies=%d roles=%d matched=%d",
167				len(policies.itemEnds), len(roles.itemEnds), len(matched.itemEnds))
168		}
169		return fixtureSites{records: records, policies: policies, roles: roles, matched: matched}
170	}
171	
172	// fixtureSites are the four counted lists in the two-record fixture.
173	type fixtureSites struct {
174		records  listSite
175		policies listSite
176		roles    listSite
177		matched  listSite
178	}
179	
180	// framePayload wraps a (possibly corrupted) payload with correct outer
181	// framing, declared length and checksum, so the failure under test is
182	// always internal list decoding rather than framing.
183	func framePayload(payload []byte) []byte {
184		out := append([]byte(nil), archiveMagic...)
185		var lb [4]byte
186		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(lb[:], uint32(len(payload)))
187		out = append(out, lb[:]...)
188		out = append(out, payload...)
189		sum := sha256.Sum256(payload)
190		return append(out, sum[:]...)
191	}
192	
193	// payloadOf extracts a copy of one archive's payload.
194	func payloadOf(t *testing.T, archive []byte) []byte {
195		t.Helper()
196		magicLen := len(archiveMagic)
197		n := int(binary.BigEndian.Uint32(archive[magicLen : magicLen+4]))
198		return append([]byte(nil), archive[magicLen+4:magicLen+4+n]...)
199	}
200	
201	// listCorruptionFixture builds complete, valid material: one policy change
202	// carrying two policies followed by one decision whose subject has two
203	// roles and whose decision matched two policies. All four counted lists
204	// therefore hold real, multi-item content.
205	func listCorruptionFixture(t *testing.T) ([]byte, []AuditRecord, Checkpoint) {
206		t.Helper()
207		s := NewStore()
208		s.Publish("acme", 0, []Policy{
209			allowPolicy("p1", "u1", "read", "org/a", false),
210			allowPolicy("p2", "u1", "read", "org/a", false),
211		})
212		req := OrgRequest{
213			SubjectOrg:  "acme",
214			ResourceOrg: "acme",
215			Subject:     Subject{ID: "u1", Roles: []string{"role-a", "role-b"}},
216			Resource:    Resource{ID: "r1", Scope: "org/a"},
217			Action:      "read",
218		}
219		original := s.Decide("acme", req)
220		recs, cp, err := s.AuditExport("acme", 0)
221		if err != nil {
222			t.Fatal(err)
223		}
224		archive, err := EncodeAuditArchive("acme", recs, cp)
225		if err != nil {
226			t.Fatal(err)
227		}
228		got, err := DecodeAuditArchive(archive, "acme", cp)
229		if err != nil {
230			t.Fatalf("fixture must decode: %v", err)
231		}
232		review, err := RecheckDecisionOffline("acme", got, cp, 2)
233		if err != nil || !review.Consistent || !reflect.DeepEqual(review.Original, original) {
234			t.Fatalf("fixture review = %+v, %v", review, err)
235		}
236		return archive, recs, cp
237	}
238	
239	// TestArchiveInternalListCountCorruption covers, for every counted list,
240	// the shapes that make a payload unreadable: a declared count the
241	// remaining bytes cannot satisfy, a count word cut off mid-read, and a
242	// complete early item followed by a later item missing a required field.
243	// All arrive with valid outer framing and checksum and must be reported as
244	// ErrInvalidArchive with nil records — even when a complete, readable
245	// prefix (a full policy change and decision) precedes the damage.
246	func TestArchiveInternalListCountCorruption(t *testing.T) {
247		good, _, cp := listCorruptionFixture(t)
248		basePayload := payloadOf(t, good)
249		sites := inspectTwoRecordPayload(t, basePayload)
250	
251		// expectInvalid runs one payload mutation and asserts the whole read
252		// fails as an unreadable archive without delivering the intact prefix.
253		// It also proves the failed call rewrites neither its input bytes nor
254		// the retained checkpoint handed to it.
255		expectInvalid := func(name, wantSubstr string, mutate func(p []byte) []byte) {
256			t.Helper()
257			payload := mutate(append([]byte(nil), basePayload...))
258			data := framePayload(payload)
259			dataSnapshot := append([]byte(nil), data...)
260			cpSnapshot := cp
261	
262			got, err := DecodeAuditArchive(data, "acme", cp)
263			if !errors.Is(err, ErrInvalidArchive) {
264				t.Fatalf("%s: err = %v, want ErrInvalidArchive", name, err)
265			}
266			if errors.Is(err, ErrInvalidRange) {
267				t.Fatalf("%s: structurally unreadable list counted as a content error: %v", name, err)
268			}
269			if got != nil {
270				t.Fatalf("%s: returned %d records on a damaged list, want nil", name, len(got))
271			}
272			if wantSubstr != "" && !strings.Contains(err.Error(), wantSubstr) {
273				t.Fatalf("%s: err = %q, want substring %q", name, err.Error(), wantSubstr)
274			}
275			if !bytes.Equal(data, dataSnapshot) {
276				t.Fatalf("%s: failed decode rewrote the archive bytes", name)
277			}
278			if cp != cpSnapshot {
279				t.Fatalf("%s: failed decode rewrote the checkpoint", name)
280			}
281		}
282	
283		lists := []struct {
284			name     string
285			site     listSite
286			minBytes int
287		}{
288			{"records", sites.records, 22},
289			{"policies", sites.policies, 6*4 + 1},
290			{"roles", sites.roles, 4},
291			{"matched", sites.matched, 4},
292		}
293	
294		for _, l := range lists {
295			// A) The count word is intact but promises more items than the bytes
296			// left could ever hold. Rewrite only the count (payload length
297			// unchanged): the read must fail as an unreadable archive, whether
298			// the per-item floor rejects the count up front or reading the
299			// missing items truncates — the error class is what the caller uses.
300			//
301			// This count value is the smallest one whose floor exceeds the
302			// remaining bytes, computed from this fixture's real offsets.
303			overCount := (len(basePayload)-(l.site.countAt+4))/l.minBytes + 1
304			expectInvalid(l.name+": count exceeds remaining items", "",
305				func(p []byte) []byte {
306					binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(p[l.site.countAt:], uint32(overCount))
307					return p
308				})
309	
310			// The maximum uint32 count on this small body must fail with the
311			// same deterministic error for every counted list, not just the
312			// record list, and without enumerating (or provisioning) the
313			// phantom items.
314			expectInvalid(l.name+": max uint32 count on small body", "implausible list count",
315				func(p []byte) []byte {
316					binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(p[l.site.countAt:], 0xffffffff)
317					return p
318				})
319	
320			// C) Every early item is whole; the final item is missing its last
321			// required field by one byte. Enough bytes remain to pass the coarse
322			// per-item count floor, so this failure must surface while reading
323			// that item — proving the item-level truncation guard, not only the
324			// count bound, is in place.
325			lastItemEnd := l.site.itemEnds[len(l.site.itemEnds)-1]
326			expectInvalid(l.name+": later item missing required field", "truncated archive payload",
327				func(p []byte) []byte { return p[:lastItemEnd-1] })
328		}
329	
330		// B) A count word physically cut off mid-read. For the three inner
331		// lists this needs a one-record payload: the outer record-count floor
332		// (22 bytes per record) must still pass so the reader actually reaches
333		// the inner list and proves its own u32 truncation guard.
334		inner := buildInnerListCountTruncationPayloads(t)
335		cutCountWord := func(name string, full []byte, countAt int) {
336			t.Helper()
337			// These are single-record payloads, so the outer record-count floor
338			// (22 bytes/record) still passes at this cut; the reader must reach
339			// the inner list and prove its own count-word truncation guard.
340			cut := countAt + 2
341			data := framePayload(full[:cut])
342			got, err := DecodeAuditArchive(data, "acme", cp)
343			if !errors.Is(err, ErrInvalidArchive) || got != nil {
344				t.Fatalf("%s: records=%v err=%v, want ErrInvalidArchive, nil", name, got, err)
345			}
346			if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "truncated archive payload") {
347				t.Fatalf("%s: err = %q, want a mid-read count truncation", name, err)
348			}
349		}
350		cutCountWord("policies count word", inner.policiesPayload, inner.policiesCountAt)
351		cutCountWord("roles count word", inner.rolesPayload, inner.rolesCountAt)
352		cutCountWord("matched count word", inner.matchedPayload, inner.matchedCountAt)
353	
354		// B for the outer record list: header complete, its count word cut.
355		headerOnly := buildArchiveHeader(t)
356		recordCountCut := append(append([]byte(nil), headerOnly...), 0x00, 0x00)
357		if got, err := DecodeAuditArchive(framePayload(recordCountCut), "acme", cp); !errors.Is(err, ErrInvalidArchive) || got != nil {
358			t.Fatalf("records count word: records=%v err=%v, want ErrInvalidArchive, nil", got, err)
359		}
360	
361		// A dedicated emphasis for the requirement: a tiny archive declaring
362		// 4294967295 records must return the deterministic error promptly,
363		// without crashing or provisioning as if the count were real.
364		w := &archiveWriter{}
365		w.stringField("acme")
366		w.u32(0)
367		w.stringField("g")
368		w.u32(0xffffffff)
369		if w.err != nil {
370			t.Fatal(w.err)
371		}
372		tinyHuge := framePayload(w.buf)
373	
374		var before, after runtime.MemStats
375		runtime.GC()
376		runtime.ReadMemStats(&before)
377		got, err := DecodeAuditArchive(tinyHuge, "acme", cp)
378		runtime.ReadMemStats(&after)
379		if !errors.Is(err, ErrInvalidArchive) || got != nil {
380			t.Fatalf("tiny archive with max count: records=%v err=%v, want ErrInvalidArchive, nil", got, err)
381		}
382		if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "implausible list count") {
383			t.Fatalf("tiny archive with max count: err = %q, want count-bound rejection", err)
384		}
385		// A regression that trusted the count would try to provision billions
386		// of records; bound what this error path may allocate.
387		if alloc := after.TotalAlloc - before.TotalAlloc; alloc > 16<<20 {
388			t.Fatalf("max-count decode allocated %d bytes, want a small error path", alloc)
389		}
390	}
391	
392	// innerListTruncation holds one complete one-record payload and the offset
393	// of a targeted inner list's count word.
394	type innerListTruncation struct {
395		policiesPayload              []byte
396		policiesCountAt              int
397		rolesPayload, matchedPayload []byte
398		rolesCountAt                 int
399		matchedCountAt               int
400	}
401	
402	// buildInnerListCountTruncationPayloads hand-builds structurally complete
403	// one-record payloads (fingerprints are irrelevant here because a truncated
404	// count fails format decoding before any content check) and reports the
405	// offset of each inner list's count word.
406	func buildInnerListCountTruncationPayloads(t *testing.T) innerListTruncation {
407		t.Helper()
408		var out innerListTruncation
409	
410		// One policy-change record whose policy list carries two policies.
411		{
412			w := &archiveWriter{}
413			w.stringField("acme")
414			w.u32(1)
415			w.stringField("g")
416			w.u32(1) // one record
417			w.stringField("acme")
418			w.u32(1)
419			w.stringField(AuditPolicyChange)
420			w.raw([]byte{archiveTagPresent}) // change present
421			w.u32(1)                         // change version
422			w.raw([]byte{archiveTagPresent}) // policy list present
423			out.policiesCountAt = len(w.buf)
424			w.u32(2)
425			w.policy(allowPolicy("p1", "u1", "read", "org/a", false))
426			w.policy(allowPolicy("p2", "u1", "read", "org/a", false))
427			w.u32(0)           // source version
428			w.boolean(false)   // rolled back
429			w.raw(nilMarker()) // decision absent
430			w.stringField("p") // prev fingerprint
431			w.stringField("f") // own fingerprint
432			if w.err != nil {
433				t.Fatal(w.err)
434			}
435			out.policiesPayload = w.buf
436		}
437	
438		// One decision record whose subject roles and decision matched list
439		// each carry two strings.
440		{
441			w := &archiveWriter{}
442			w.stringField("acme")
443			w.u32(1)
444			w.stringField("g")
445			w.u32(1) // one record
446			w.stringField("acme")
447			w.u32(1)
448			w.stringField(AuditDecision)
449			w.raw([]byte{archiveTagNil})     // change absent
450			w.raw([]byte{archiveTagPresent}) // decision present
451			w.stringField("acme")            // SubjectOrg
452			w.stringField("acme")            // ResourceOrg
453			w.stringField("u1")              // subject ID
454			w.stringField("user")            // subject kind
455			w.raw([]byte{archiveTagPresent}) // roles present
456			out.rolesCountAt = len(w.buf)
457			w.u32(2)
